    x<-subset(x,select=-c(iso2c, region, income, lending))

    x[complete.cases(x),]
}

messages.subject: R shiny server failed to run with apache proxy due to connection issue with certain websocket
messages.subject_clean: R shiny server failed to run with apache proxy due to connection issue with certain websocket
messages.body_plain:
I set up the R shiny server with a apache proxy. The server will accept request from port 80 and forward it to port 3838

In my virtue host file I have the following:

        ProxyPass /shinyport/ http://localhost:3838/
        ProxyPassReverse /shinyport/ http://localhost:3838/
        RedirectMatch permanent ^/shinyport$ /shinyport/

and I have set up the R shiny configuration file accordingly, too

       server {
          listen 3838 127.0.0.1;
          .......
       }

However, when I run the R shiny app (in the directory of testapp under site_dir ) from firefox, the interface can be shown then it stop short with error message in java log:

Firefox can't establish a connection to the server at ws://[myservername]/shinyport/testapp/__sockjs__/883/iy9jjfoj/websocket.

I searched on line and found a similar experience  https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/219
which I followed and added the following in my virtue host configuration file

        <LocationMatch ^/testapp/_sockjs_/([0-9]+)/([a-z0-9]+)/websocket$>
                ProxyPassMatch ws://localhost:3838/testapp/_sockjs_/$1/$2/websocket
        </LocationMatch>

messages.subject: Re: CairoPDF in downloadHandler
messages.subject_clean: CairoPDF in downloadHandler
messages.body_plain:
Sorry for the lack of reply earlier.

I just looked at your example app, the problem is that CairoPDF takes the file1 path and automatically appends ".pdf" to it. So the PDF data ends up being written to the wrong filename, and when Shiny goes to read file1 it doesn't find it.

Adding this line to the end of your handler fixes it:

if (file.exists(paste0(file1, ".pdf")))
  file.rename(paste0(file1, ".pdf"), file1)

messages.body_plain:
Hi folks -- is there a "static" output version of DataTables 1.10.x available through Shiny or another library? Ramnath was very kind to add an interface to rCharts a year ago but this uses 1.9.x. This will help reduce the load on our Shiny server, having static options for some tables.

Thanks,

AT

On Monday, August 25, 2014 6:06:42 PM UTC-4, Yihui Xie wrote:
> Hi,
>
> We just integrated the new version of the DataTables library (1.10.2)
> into the development version of shiny. Due to the tremendous changes
> in parameter names from DataTables 1.9.x to 1.10.x, we want to make
> sure DataTables 1.10.2 still works reasonably well in shiny. If you
> are interested in testing the development version, please install it
> via:
>
>   if (!require("devtools")) install.packages("devtools")
>   devtools::install_github(c("rstudio/htmltools", "rstudio/shiny"))
>
> A guide for upgrading parameter names from DT 1.9.x to 1.10.x is here:
> https://datatables.net/upgrade/1.10-convert We have tried to
> automatically correct some of the old parameter names in shiny, but
> this automatic correction certainly won't work for all use cases,
> especially if you have deeply customized your DataTables using
> complicated JavaScript options. You can see
> https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/commit/6f2a5618 for examples
> of converting DT 1.9 names to 1.10 names.
>
> Please let us know if you have any comments or questions. Thanks!
>
> Regards,
> Yihui

Yes, that is the only one JS error I got.

OK, I did some research on this. I changed the code below in my JS file and get it work.

(old)

var barmin=$('#slider-jq').slider('values',0);
    Shiny.onInputChange("jq",barmin);

(new)

 var barmin=$('#slider-jq').slider('values',0);

   setTimeout(function(){ Shiny.onInputChange("jq",barmin);},0);

It seems it has to wait for Shiny loading 'shiny.js' or something that has "Shiny.onInputChange' defined. Without wait time by setTimeout, Shiny.onInputChange cannot be recognized. Do you think this is the reason why my previous code does not work?

Thanks.

messages.body_plain: I am trying to put some order in my code because I need to implement a huge application and I am creating functions from chunks of code to improve readibility and favour reuse. I have an issue when trying to do so with renderTable. My original call cannot be fully converted to a function, the renderTable must stay outside: renderResults <- function(objectives) { # renderTable({ d<-data.frame(Result=objectives) d<-format(d,big.mark=",", scientific=FALSE) d[,1]<-paste('$',d[,1]) d[1,]<-paste("",d[1,],"") rownames(d)[1]<-paste("",rownames(d)[1],"") d # }, align='lr',sanitize.text.function = function(x) x) } and be called: output$results <- renderTable({ renderResults(scalc()$Objectives) }, align='lr',sanitize.text.function = function(x) x) what is not exactly what I wanted because I need to set the options each time. I have also tried with observe aassuming that someone needs to check when scalc(), that is reactive, changes but they don't work either. Is there any way to improve this? What is so special on renderXXX functions that this doesn't work? I guess is related to scoping but I don't get it. I have managed to solve it including output$results generation inside scalc() but only works if I keep another output that I generate from scalc() using renderDataTable outside scalc(). If both outputs are generated inside then I get no output. There are only two outputs in the app. The second output generated with renderDataTable depends on another reactive variable: change() Both variables get triggered from the same button. I suspect the outputs are by default also reactive element that requires a trigger. I know it's a bit confusing, I can try to prepare a minimum code that helps to reproduce the problem. I am using R 3.1.1 on R studio 0.98, with shiny 0.10.0 and Windows 7

messages.subject: Dynamic webpage using shiny
messages.subject_clean: Dynamic webpage using shiny
messages.body_plain:
How to make dynamic webpage using shiny with new uploading data and to  make dynamic change in plot
and make change aromatically in every field ?
 If you know then give answer the question.
Thanks!

library(shiny)
runApp(list(
  ui = pageWithSidebar(

    headerPanel("Data Analysis Dashboard"),

    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput('file1', 'Choose file to upload',
                accept = c(
                  'text/csv',
                  'text/comma-separated-values',
                  'text/tab-separated-values',
                  'text/plain',
                  '.csv',
                  '.tsv'
                )
      ),
      tags$hr(),
      checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE),
      radioButtons('sep', 'Separator',
                   c(Comma=',',
                     Semicolon=';',
                     Tab='\t'),
                   ','),
      radioButtons('quote', 'Quote',
                   c(None='',
                     'Double Quote'='"',
                     'Single Quote'="'"),
                   '"'),

      selectInput(
        "plotType", "Plot Type",
        c(Scatter = "scatter",
          Histogram = "hist",
          Bargraph = "barplot",
          lineChart ="lines",
          Piechart = "pie")),

      # Only show this panel if the plot type is a histogram
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = "input.plotType == 'hist'",
        selectInput(
          "breaks", "Breaks",
          c("Sturges",
            "Scott",
            "Freedman-Diaconis",
            "[Custom]" = "custom")),
        # Only show this panel if Custom is selected
        conditionalPanel(
          condition = "input.breaks == 'custom'",
          sliderInput("breakCount", "Break Count", min=1, max=1000, value=10)
        )
      ),
      sliderInput("n",
                  "Number of observations:",
                  value = 500,
                  min = 1,
                  max = 1000)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot")),
        tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary")),
        tabPanel("Table", tableOutput("contents"))

      )

    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    data <- reactive({
      plotType <- switch(input$plotType,
                         scatter = scatter,
                         hist = hist,
                         barplot = barplot,
                         lines = lines,
                         pie=pie,
                         rnorm)

      plotType(input$n)
    })
    output$contents <- renderTable({

      inFile <- input$file1

      if (is.null(inFile))
        return(NULL)

      read.csv(inFile$datapath, header = input$header,
               sep = input$sep, quote = input$quote)
    })
   # output$hist <- renderPlot(
    #  hist(Histogram, breaks = input$n,
     #      col = "skyblue", border = "white")
    #)

    output$plot <- renderPlot({
      plotType <- input$plotType
      n <- input$n

      hist(data(),
           main=paste('r', plotType, '(', n, ')', sep=''))
    })

    output$summary <- renderPrint({
      summary(data())
    })

    output$table <- renderTable({
      data.frame(x=data())
    })

  }
))

Hi,

In my shiny app (http://comet.epigen.kcl.ac.uk:3838/comet/), I create first a png image and after that, I ask if they want to download the file.
The format of file could be png, pdf, eps format.

My problem is that the creation of plot takes a little time and if I ask to produce the pdf file, I have an error message because the connection is stopped.

I tried to increase the session time in the configuration file, but I have error message to run my app

app_init_timeout 3600;
app_idle_timeout 3600;

Do you have idea to create pdf or eps  file ?
Do you have idea to extend the session time  to create a file with downloadbutton?

This is my function

output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() { paste(input$plotfilename, input$imageformat, sep='.') },
    content = function(filename) {
      if(input$imageformat == "pdf"){
        pdf(encoding = "ISOLatin1.enc",
            file = filenameImage,
            onefile=FALSE,
            width=as.numeric(input$imagesize),
            height=as.numeric(input$imagesize),
            paper="special")
      }
      if(input$imageformat == "eps"){
        postscript(encoding = "ISOLatin1.enc",
                   file = filenameImage,
                   horizontal=FALSE,
                   onefile=FALSE,
                   width=as.numeric(input$imagesize),
                   height=as.numeric(input$imagesize),
                   paper="special",
                   pagecentre=TRUE,
                   fonts=c("sans"))
      }
      if(input$imageformat == "png"){
        png(file = filenameImage,
            width=as.numeric(input$imagesize),
            height=as.numeric(input$imagesize),
            fonts=c("sans"))
      }
      #lena = readImage(filenameImage)
      #display(lena)
      cometplotPrint()
      dev.off()
    }
  )

Shoot. I think you're hitting a hard-coded timeout in Shiny Server:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/lib/main.js#L185

Is there any way that your code could be refactored using reactive expressions so that the results of the calculation can be shared between the in-app plot and the file download? messages.subject: Re: multiple dynamic plots in shiny
messages.subject_clean: multiple dynamic plots in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Your renderUI should be returning something more like `lapply(fields, plotOutput)`, while each renderPlot should be assigned to a corresponding `output[[fieldName]]`. If possible, you should do the latter outside of the renderUI (unless you can't predict all possible fields in advance). It's OK to have these output[[fieldName]] defined even if the corresponding plotOutput is not visible at the moment on the page; they will generally be smart enough not to execute when they're not currently on the page.

messages.subject: How to update a reactiveValues object?

messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody!

I have a pair of auxiliary inputs that allows user to choose combinations from a set of choices. Also, it is convenient one to be able to remove an item that was created before.

For this task, a named list, in the form of reactiveValues object, listN <- reactiveValues(), will be in charge to store these information.

The function to ADD items is working like a charm, but when I try to REMOVE items from listN, its item names persists forever!

My strategy was make use of reactiveValuesToList(), manipulate its items and replace listN with a brand new instance of reactiveValues() (or do.call(reactiveValues, listN_as_list).

I stored a reproducible app at Gist. I hope it is sufficient to you guys help me out. Please insist in more clarification if needed.

URL:

gist.github.com/d43e72959c4576d27535 <http://gist.github.com/d43e72959c4576d27535>

Code to run on console:

shiny::runGist('d43e72959c4576d27535')

Thanks in advance!

PS: Shiny is an awesome feature, congratulations and thank you!

messages.subject: Re: How to update a reactiveValues object?
messages.subject_clean: How to update a reactiveValues object?
messages.body_plain:
Yeah, you can't replace an entire reactiveValues instance like that and expect anything that's bound to the previous reactiveValues instance to instantly know about the new one. The slots on the reactiveValues instance itself are reactive, but its own variable is not.

I think the real issue here is that, unlike lists and envs, you can't remove values from reactiveValues, only set them to NULL.

There are two easy workarounds I can think of:
In addition to the reactiveValues instance's slots being reactive, also make the variable reactive, using makeReactiveBinding.
You could also use reactiveValues as normal, but keep a list IN the reactiveValues that holds the combinations, not having the reactiveValues itself hold the values. In other words, values <- reactiveValues(combos = list()), and when something new gets added, values$combos[[x]] <- y.
In trying out fix #1 above, I found that updateSelectInput doesn't work properly when choices is a length-0 vector. Instead of sending a 0-length vector to the client, it doesn't send anything for choices at all, so the choices never change.

I've forked your gist and added two revisions: one that implements workaround #1 (along with some other problems I found), and one that works around the updateSelectInput issue by using renderUI.
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/eaedfed5095d37217fca/revisions

messages.subject: Re: Issue with numericInput
messages.subject_clean: Issue with numericInput
messages.body_plain:
You've created a preferences reactive expression for the sole purpose of setting a "score" variable. You don't want to do that (basically ever); instead, rename the preferences reactive "score" instead, and just have it return input$Cost*x. A properly written reactive expression is interesting for the value it returns, and nothing else--no side effects.

Secondly, if you create a reactive expression and don't call it from anywhere, it's just as useless as if you create a function and don't call it from anywhere. You want to cbind(college, score()), but do it inside of renderDataTable, not directly inside the function(input,output). If you have it directly inside the function, it won't ever re-execute as the value of score() changes--and in fact since this is such a common mistake for Shiny beginners, we actually throw an error if you try to read a reactive expression outside of either an output renderer, a reactive expression, or an observer.

Final code should look like this:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  score = reactive ({
    if (input$Outstate == TRUE) {
      diff = input$FundsAvailable - college$Out.of.state.tuition
    }
    else {
      diff = input$FundsAvailable - college$In.state.tuition
    }
    x = ifelse(diff <= -20000, 10, ifelse(diff <= -10000, 8, ifelse(diff <= 0, 6,0)))
    input$Cost * x
  })
  output$school = renderDataTable({
    college = cbind(college, score())
    ...

messages.subject: Re: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
messages.subject_clean: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
messages.body_plain:
1) I'd move the "input$action != oldaction" block out of output$history, and into a separate observe({...}). Let output$history focus on rendering that text.

2) buildhistory here is just a normal R variable, not a reactive one. Shiny's reactive expressions and outputs only know to calculate when their reactive dependencies change; it doesn't magically know what R variables are interesting to reactivity. You can add this call right before or after you first declare buildhistory: makeReactiveBinding("buildhistory"). Or if you have a bunch of reactive values to read/write, you could consider using reactiveValues() instead; it declares a list-like object where reading/writing values to it triggers reactivity.

3) The statement "buildhistory <- append(buildhistory, ...)" will trigger an endless chain reaction. You need to do this: "buildhistory <- append(isolate(buildhistory), ...)" so that your observe() block knows that it doesn't want to automatically re-execute when buildhistory changes (since it, itself, is about to change buildhistory).

messages.subject: "Page Not Found" for some users but not all
messages.subject_clean: "Page Not Found" for some users but not all
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I'm past what I can easily diagnose because it's not an issue I can reproduce on my machines, so I could use some more tips for how to diagnose these problems, or perhaps they're known issues.

The gist of it: I'm running a whole suite of Shiny apps that appear at war-on-ice.com <http://war-on-ice.com>, through a back-end server (vincerdata.com <http://vincerdata.com>) and iframes. For most users, there is no problem. For two (who happen to be heavy users) there are issues where nothing at all loads.

Here are the issues I've been able to glean:

1) Sometimes the static elements in ui.R alone load -- not the elements cooked up in server.R and passed to ui.R, like

onload.seasongcode <- reactive (something here)
 output$onload.seasongcode <-
        renderUI (textInput (inputId="seasongcode", label="Game ID", value = onload.seasongcode()))

2) Sometimes nothing loads at all, and the Javascript pops up with this

 <https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/-aHmUnm860dQ/VGGSi8AZkhI/AAAAAAAAAZg/o-pfJ7g9QYk/s1600/cEKqMs3o.png>
so I asked one of my users to do this and try the diagnostics, and he said

"they're all returning 404 not found errors when it attempts to access the JSON or the bootstrap.css.map"

I fixed the bootstrap.css.map issue but that seems to be unrelated to the Shiny, since that's in the containing page.

3) For one of these users, the issue only just started yesterday. I don't think he changed anything along the way, so it might be a ports issue from his ISP. I should note that I have the shiny server running on port 80 already.

Any insight would be appreciated.

AT

Hi Cheng,

Rserve is a TCP/IP server which allows other programs to use facilities of R (see www.r-project.org <http://www.r-project.org/>) from various languages without the need to initialize R or link against Rlibrary. Every connection has a separate workspace and working directory. Client-side implementations are available for popular languages such as C/C++, PHP and Java.Rserve supports remote connection, authentication and file transfer. Typical use is to integrate R backend for computation of statstical models, plots etc. in other applications.

So let's assume our server is running on 127.0.0.1:8080 <http://127.0.0.1:8080> and sends httpresponse as html/json . Under our application(allows r code to run on web interface) we need to run shiny app.

we have written wrapper(r function) around shiny to use shiny as it is. Works well if shinysession is not involved in rendering component.

Okay, you were using shiny 0.9.1, four versions behind the latest one
(same thing for the R version). I'm not quite sure if you need to
upgrade R/R packages, since you use DataTables extensively, and
DataTables has been upgraded to 1.10.x
(http://blog.rstudio.org/2014/10/02/shiny-0-10-2/), which may or may
not break your tables, depending on how much you used custom
initialization options. You may try to upgrade R and R packages
locally, and see if all the tables still work well.

I believe the original problem was an R problem, even though it was
manifested in JS/HTML. There have been a few bug fixes since shiny
0.9.1, which might be relevant.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Loading apps from memory
messages.subject_clean: Loading apps from memory
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm working to optimize the load time on my apps. Right now, when a user accesses it, it takes about 3-4 seconds for the app to read the .csv file containing the data and then display the graphs via the googleVis package. Say the .csv is automatically generated (by some cron job). I'm aware that the load time can be faster if the .csv file were loaded into memory and kept into memory, so when the user accesses the app, then the app would load the data from memory as opposed to reading from the file. This would likely result in an instantaneous load of the app.

I hope this makes sense. Does anyone have an idea how I can approach this?

Alan

messages.subject: Re: Loading apps from memory
messages.subject_clean: Loading apps from memory
messages.body_plain:
Assuming you have a cronjob hat already dumps the csv data, I'd suggest another cronjob that loads R, processes the new CSV data, and saves an RData file.

The shiny script then loads the RData file.

Steps

1. Create Rscript file that processes your CSV and saves to RData file (See: http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/Rscript.html)
2. Set up cronjob to execute the Rscript every 10 minutes or whatever makes sense.
3. Alter your shiny script to load the RData file saved by cron. ....    load(savedData.RData)
4. Profit

Erik

On Monday, November 10, 2014 3:46:50 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> 1) I'd move the "input$action != oldaction" block out of output$history, and into a separate observe({...}). Let output$history focus on rendering that text.
>
> 2) buildhistory here is just a normal R variable, not a reactive one. Shiny's reactive expressions and outputs only know to calculate when their reactive dependencies change; it doesn't magically know what R variables are interesting to reactivity. You can add this call right before or after you first declare buildhistory: makeReactiveBinding("buildhistory"). Or if you have a bunch of reactive values to read/write, you could consider using reactiveValues() instead; it declares a list-like object where reading/writing values to it triggers reactivity.
>
> 3) The statement "buildhistory <- append(buildhistory, ...)" will trigger an endless chain reaction. You need to do this: "buildhistory <- append(isolate(buildhistory), ...)" so that your observe() block knows that it doesn't want to automatically re-execute when buildhistory changes (since it, itself, is about to change buildhistory).

messages.subject: Re: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
messages.subject_clean: Persistent variable problem -- I *think* I'm defining it in the right scope, but not working
messages.body_plain:
It's probably just the normal R scoping behavior you're seeing.

a <- 10
makeReactiveBinding("a")
a <- 20 # does trigger reactivity
foo <- function() {
  a <- 30 # doesn't trigger reactivity; this just creates a NEW variable inside this function's scope
  a <<- 30 # this does assign our original variable and triggers reactivity
}
foo()

Render expressions, observers, reactive expressions, etc. all introduce their own scopes just like functions do, so if you want to assign to variables in parent scopes you need to use <<-.

"Revolution R Open can work side-by-side with any other version of R. During installation, a symbolic link is created under /usr/bin/ that points to the last version of R that was installed, in this case Revolution R Open. In order to continue working with a different version of R than the last installed from a terminal window, you must specify the full path to the R executable you want to use."

http://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/installation/#tab-W1RE08s2H-0

I presume this means that Shiny will also just use the latest version of R that was installed on the hosting server, as per the symbolic link under /usr/bin.

I don't know is this would be at all possible for an app hosted by shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, but I can't see how it would be unless those guys has installed ORR (which is a question to ask in this group I suppose: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shinyapps-users)

messages.subject: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?
messages.subject_clean: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Would someone please let me know why you cannot use an output element more than once, please?

Using the Shiny "census-app" as an example, why is it that using "text2" is only allowed once, please?  Why does that element disappear after use?

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

     output$text1 <- renderText({
          paste("You have selected", input$var)
     })

output$text2 <- renderText({
          paste("You have chosen a range that goes from ",input$range[1]," to ", input$range[2])
     })

  }
)

ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("censusVis"),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      helpText("Create demographic maps with
        information from the 2010 US Census."),

      selectInput("var",
        label = "Choose a variable to display",
        choices = c("Percent White", "Percent Black",
          "Percent Hispanic", "Percent Asian"),
        selected = "Percent White"),

      sliderInput("range",
        label = "Range of interest:",
        min = 0, max = 100, value = c(0, 100))
    ),

    mainPanel(
      textOutput("text1"),
 br(),
 textOutput("text2"),
 br(),

          # App will not run because of this second use of "text2"
          textOutput("text2"),

messages.subject: Re: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?
messages.subject_clean: Why can't you use an output more than once, please?
messages.body_plain:
There are classes of outputs that can't be represented twice in the same page. For example, renderPlot by default will use the width of the output to determine what size to render the plot at; if there were multiple outputs then that wouldn't work.

And from an implementation perspective, we map these output IDs to HTML element IDs, and HTML element IDs must be unique.

messages.body_plain:
Does it matter that the calculation happens twice? If so, because these calculations take a long time to run, it might be desirable to add an explicit "Calculate" button, so you're not automatically recalculating each time the user selects or deselects a column. If you decide to do that, you'll want to avoid the submitButton() function (it doesn't work right with file inputs) and use actionButton instead. There's an article here <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/isolation.html> but feel free to ask if it's not clear how you would apply that to your app.

If you want to avoid a calculate button, you could work around this a bit painfully by putting in a high-priority observer that basically detects each time a file is uploaded and sets a flag that tells the reactives to ignore the uploaded file until the column information is also uploaded. Something like this (my additions in bold):

test_func<-function(data_raw){
  print (nrow(data_raw))
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  values <- reactiveValues(waitForColumns = FALSE)
  observe(priority = 10, {
    input$file1
    values$waitForColumns <- TRUE
  })
  observe({
    input$columns
    values$waitForColumns <- FALSE
  })

  dataInput <- reactive({
    inFile <- input$file1
    if (is.null(inFile)) return(NULL)

    data_load_all<-read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=T, sep=',', quote='"', stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
    data_load<-subset(data_load_all, select=c(input$show_vars))
    data_study<-unique(data_load$Col2)
    return (list("data_load_all"=data_load_all, "data_load"=data_load, "data_study"=data_study))
  })

  study<-reactive({
    if (is.null(dataInput()$data_study))
      return ()

    validate(need(!values$waitForColumns, FALSE))

    all_citation<-dataInput()$data_load$Col2
    if (is.null(input$columns)) return()
    study_choose<-unlist(lapply(input$columns,  function(x) which(all_citation==x)))
    print (c('all_citation=', all_citation))
    print (c('input$columns=', input$columns))
    print (c('study_choose=', study_choose))
    test<-test_func(dataInput()$data_load_all[study_choose, ])
    return (list("study_choose"=study_choose))
  })

  output$contents <- renderDataTable({
    study_choose_temp<-study()$study_choose
    dataInput()$data_load[study_choose_temp,]
    }
  )

   output$study <- renderUI({
    # If missing input, return to avoid error later in function
    if(is.null(dataInput()$data_study)) return()

    # Create the checkboxes and select them all by default
    checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose studies to plot",
                        choices  = dataInput()$data_study,
                        selected = dataInput()$data_study)
  })

messages.subject_clean: How to store(save) multiple objects inside a reactive element and use them further
messages.body_plain:
You should make them all reactive expressions (you would access the values of val.both1 using val.both1() and likewise for val.both2).

vars <- reactive({
  list(model = names(a()), observation = names(b()))
})
var.both1 <- reactive({
  c(vars()$model, vars()$observation)
})
var.both2 <- reactive({
  Reduce(intersect,list(vars()$model, vars()$observation))
})

Sure. I think `.change()` is similar to your suggested  `validate` function. Maybe something like:

   run `study_choose<-unlist(lapply(input$columns,  function(x) which(all_citation==x)))`;
});

The reason is an early fired `renderUI` will generate a data framework with different number of rows...  Most of the columns of this data frame comes from CSV, but there a several hard coded columns. I guess I can also set an exception rule on the data frame part. So may I know why `renderUI` is running twice?

messages.subject: Re: Where is the data stored when I run a shiny application?
messages.subject_clean: Where is the data stored when I run a shiny application?
messages.body_plain:
It all depends on how you are running your app. If you're calling shiny::runApp from your R session or hitting the "Run App" button in RStudio, then everything is run locally on your machine--we don't send anything to our servers.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny R Reactive Function Fired Twice
messages.subject_clean: Shiny R Reactive Function Fired Twice
messages.body_plain:
The reason isn't that renderUI is running too fast. If anything it's too "slow" (I put it in quotes because it couldn't possibly happen faster). When a new file is uploaded, dataInput, study, output$contents, and output$study all become invalidated and need to run. That all happens; this is the first run, when nrow == 0. Now output$study has run, the browser's UI updates with a new set of columns, and since they're all selected by default, now a new value for input$columns is sent to the server. That causes study and output$contents to become invalidated and need to run. When that happens, it's the second run, when nrow == 13 or whatever.

That's why my solution says, when input$file changes, don't actually let study execute. Only when input$columns changes is study allowed to execute. So what you were asking for (jquery change()) actually exists, it's just called observe() in Shiny, and my proposed changes include that.

messages.body_plain:
There is one problem in the observer-based solution I sent you, I'm not sure how to fix it without adding some JS. That is, uploading two files which both contain the same set of columns, one after another, will not work; the second won't update because if input$columns is set to the same value, the observer won't fire at all.

Is the button approach problematic?

On Mon, Nov 17, 2014 at 1:33 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> The reason isn't that renderUI is running too fast. If anything it's too "slow" (I put it in quotes because it couldn't possibly happen faster). When a new file is uploaded, dataInput, study, output$contents, and output$study all become invalidated and need to run. That all happens; this is the first run, when nrow == 0. Now output$study has run, the browser's UI updates with a new set of columns, and since they're all selected by default, now a new value for input$columns is sent to the server. That causes study and output$contents to become invalidated and need to run. When that happens, it's the second run, when nrow == 13 or whatever.
>
> That's why my solution says, when input$file changes, don't actually let study execute. Only when input$columns changes is study allowed to execute. So what you were asking for (jquery change()) actually exists, it's just called observe() in Shiny, and my proposed changes include that.
>
> On Mon, Nov 17, 2014 at 1:16 PM, tao hong <hongt...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > The reason is an early fired `renderUI` will generate a data framework with different number of rows...  Most of the columns of this data frame comes from CSV, but there a several hard coded columns. I guess I can also set an exception rule on the data frame part. So may I know why `renderUI` is running twice?

If you decide to do that, you'll want to avoid the submitButton() function (it doesn't work right with file inputs) and use actionButton instead. Wow, thanks for the step by step explanation and I do agree your proposed method fixed the issue. Thanks for your help!

On Monday, November 17, 2014 4:34:22 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> The reason isn't that renderUI is running too fast. If anything it's too "slow" (I put it in quotes because it couldn't possibly happen faster). When a new file is uploaded, dataInput, study, output$contents, and output$study all become invalidated and need to run. That all happens; this is the first run, when nrow == 0. Now output$study has run, the browser's UI updates with a new set of columns, and since they're all selected by default, now a new value for input$columns is sent to the server. That causes study and output$contents to become invalidated and need to run. When that happens, it's the second run, when nrow == 13 or whatever.
>
> That's why my solution says, when input$file changes, don't actually let study execute. Only when input$columns changes is study allowed to execute. So what you were asking for (jquery change()) actually exists, it's just called observe() in Shiny, and my proposed changes include that.
>
> On Mon, Nov 17, 2014 at 1:16 PM, tao hong <hongt...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > The reason is an early fired `renderUI` will generate a data framework with different number of rows...  Most of the columns of this data frame comes from CSV, but there a several hard coded columns. I guess I can also set an exception rule on the data frame part. So may I know why `renderUI` is running twice?

messages.subject: Possible to output R code that Shiny runs?
messages.subject_clean: Possible to output R code that Shiny runs?
messages.body_plain:
I have a rather extensive Shiny app, the main purpose of which is to provide social science researchers with a specific set of analysis tools without requiring knowledge of the R command line. Since it would be impossible to capture all of the power and flexibility of R in a web app (though Shiny has been very impressive so far), I would like to provide my users with the option of transitioning into the command line. Specifically, I want them to be able to see the R code that Shiny runs as a result of their interaction with the app.

Is there any functionality in Shiny or other packages that would allow me to do this?

I am aware of the shinyAce package: https://github.com/trestletech/shinyAce
which is a viable option, except that it would require me to call updateAceEditor("editorid", value="newcode...") anytime one of my reactive objects changes. I would be re-writing code that already exists, almost doubling the length of my server.R file.

Ideally, I'm looking for something that can capture the R commands that shiny runs as they happen and recognize when they change. Does this exist?

Thanks,
Emily

When the users wants to replicate the analysis they call the regular functions directly by knit-ing the Rmd document from within the app.

messages.subject: How to show data on top of an image in shiny
messages.subject_clean: How to show data on top of an image in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to display (and dynamically change) data displayed in an R-Shiny App.  I can do the plotting on an image (without shiny and without dynamic control) as described here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/12918367/in-r-how-to-plot-with-a-png-as-background>.  How can I do this in R shiny?  Here is what I have so far (I am yet to implement dynamic control).

This raises an error in the Server.R code at "lim<-par()".  I am new to R and to shiny, so this may be a simple mistake and easy fix (I hope so.)

Thanks in advance,
Dustin

[Server.R]

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(png)

ima <- readPNG("my_image.png")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

     output$text1 <- renderText({
          "You have selected this"
     })
  output$plot <- {
     return(
     plot(c(1, 2), c(2, 1))
     lim<-par()
     rasterImage(ima, lim$usr[1], lim$usr[3], lim$usr[2], lim$usr[4])
     lines(c(1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 1.8, 2.0), c(1, 1.3, 1.7, 1.6, 1.7, 1.0), type="b", lwd=5, col="white")
     )
     }
}
)

[ui.R]

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Dynamic Data Display"),

  fluidRow(

    column(3,
      selectInput("day", label = h3("Select weekday"),
        choices = list("Monday" = 1, "Tuesday" = 2,
                       "Wednesday" = 3, "Thursday" = 4,
    "Friday" = 5, "Saturday" = 6,
    "Sunday" = 7), selected = 1)),

    column(3,
      sliderInput("Time", label = h3("Select time"),
        min = 0, max = 23, value = 8))

  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("plot")
  )
))

messages.body_plain:
Dear Fereshteh
Thanks for your reply to my topic. Yes the ProxyPass has no problem and request from port 80 can be successfully forwarded to port 3838 on the server as I was able to open the R shiny app page.

The issue lies in the the subsequent execution of my R app in which it needs communication with the user side through websockets (probably because I was using a the ggplot2 library in my R app).
The error message I encountered is

Firefox can't establish a connection to the server at ws://[myservername]/shinyport/testapp/__sockjs__/883/iy9jjfoj/websocket.

Then I tried to address the issue by adding a regular expression ProxyPassMatch, inspired from the solution proposed in https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/219

<LocationMatch ^/testapp/_sockjs_/([0-9]+)/([a-z0-9]+)/websocket$>

                ProxyPassMatch ws://localhost:3838/testapp/_sockjs_/$1/$2/websocket
</LocationMatch>

Still, it does not work...basically port 80 can successfully forward user request to port 3838 but the subsequent websocket communication cannot established..

Is there a way to get around this problem?

Thanks a lot

I tweaked your output$uiOutputPanel like this (changes in bold):

    output$uiOutputPanel <- renderUI({
      input$sentence # Just the act of reading input$sentence will cause this block to re-execute
      word1 <- sample(state.name <http://state.name>, 1)
      button1Click <- paste("$('#sentence').val($('#sentence').val() + ' ", word1, "').trigger('change')", sep='')

      tags$button(type="button", id="word1", word1, class="btn action-button shiny-bound-input" ,
        onclick=button1Click)

messages.body_plain:
Good morning,

Full disclosure: I posted about this issue earlier on Stackoverflow (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26999336/shiny-includehtml-not-playing-nicely-with-navbarmenu), but didn't get a reply. Before I throw the towel, I thought I'd give it one last try on the shiny discussion group.

Let's consider a simple shiny application with server.R and ui.R file. I'm just modifying RStudio's shiny template slightly:

server.R:

    library(shiny)

    shinyServer(function(input, output) {

      output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

        # generate bins based on input$bins from ui.R
        x    <- faithful[, 2]
        bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)

        # draw the histogram with the specified number of bins
        hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')

      })

    })

Now, as to the ui.R, I want to include two HTML files. These are generated by R Markdown -- the simple shiny template would do just fine as sample document -- and I'll just call them test1 and test2. The code is as follows:

    library(shiny)
    path1 <- "test1"
    path2 <- "test2"

    shinyUI(fluidPage(

      # Application title
      titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),

      # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          sliderInput("bins",
                      "Number of bins:",
                      min = 1,
                      max = 50,
                      value = 30)
        ),

         # Show a plot of the generated distribution
        mainPanel(
          tabsetPanel(id="tabs",
                      tabPanel("One",
                               plotOutput("distPlot")
                      ),
                     # navbarMenu("Simulation Features",
                                 tabPanel("Two",
                                          HTML("Test"),
                                          includeHTML(path1)
                                 ),
                                 tabPanel("Three",
                                          includeHTML(path2)
                                 )
                    #  )
        ))
      )
    ))

Note that the navbarMenu line (and the corresponding closing bracket) is commented out. This code runs as expected on both Windows and Mac, as well as on shiny server.

However, if I uncomment the navbarMenu line, then the code only runs on the Mac. On Windows and shiny server, the navigation becomes unresponsible, i.e. you can click as much as you want, nothing happens.

messages.body_plain:
The UI you specify in ui.R is rendered completely when the app loads. So anything that's data-dependent like this has to come from the server. You have two options:

1) Have these selectInputs start out with empty vectors for their choices. Then in your server.R, assuming you have a reactive(...) called "data", set up observers like this:
observe({
  if (!is.null(data()))
    updateSelectInput(session, "Client", choices = data()$Carrier)
})
Do this once for each dynamic select input.

2) Take out the interior of this tabPanel and replace it with a uiOutput("tab3"), and on the server side, have output$tab3 <- renderOutput({...}) that dynamically generates this UI. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html

Xiao,

A couple of things you can try:

1- In your browser access your Shiny application and then try these keyboard combinations: Ctrl+Alt+Shint+A
This would show you a list of protocols (network methods) and their status (enabled or disabled). In my case I have all of them enabled. So if there is any problem with websockets, it can default to another protocol. If you see the non-websockets protocols as disabled, please enable and try again.

2- You can also use this configuration in your /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf file:

disable_websockets;

Restart your Shiny Server and try again.

Let us know if neither of these solves the problem for you.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Multiple Plots from a Single Command
messages.subject_clean: Multiple Plots from a Single Command
messages.body_plain:
I have recently been playing with Shiny and love it.  It is really very easy to do simple things quickly.  I have a situation that I am not sure how to move forward with.  I have an Rcpp function that returns two data frames to me.  I would like to generate two plots based on these two separate data frames.  The inputs for the routine are basically matched for the two data frames.  This means that if I change one variable, then both plots would need to be updated.  As I understand it I must have each individual plot inside its own reactive environment.  This means that I would need to execute the Rcpp function twice, one for each plot.  As this function takes a while to run I would like to avoid that.  Is there a way to have a function execute inside of a reactive environment and then that output be shared with two separate renderPlot environments?  I think the server function would be something like:

sourceCpp('../calculatePercentClearenceParallel.cpp')

shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {

    # This would include the variables that affect both plots and would execute the long running function (myFunction)
    output$rp1 = renderNull({
      mslope = tan(input$slider_mslope*((2*pi)/360))

      tpc = myFunction(nm = nm)
    })

    # This would include the variables that affect this plot only and would not need to execute the long running function...
    output$rp1 = renderPlot({
      mslope = tan(input$slider_mslope*((2*pi)/360))

      pdata = tpc$PCData1

      rp = ggplot(pdata) + theme_bw() +
        geom_tile(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, fill = pc)) +
        geom_contour(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, z = smoothpc), breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8), color = 'red') +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = range(pdata$slopes), ylim = range(pdata$intercepts))
      rp
    })

    output$rp2 = renderPlot({
      mslope = tan(input$slider_mslope*((2*pi)/360))

      pdata = tpc$PCData2

      rp = ggplot(pdata) + theme_bw() +
        geom_tile(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, fill = pc)) +
        geom_contour(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, z = smoothpc), breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8), color = 'red') +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = range(pdata$slopes), ylim = range(pdata$intercepts))
      rp
    })
  }
)

I think that I am curious if there can be a common environment and then an execution graph that is established for variable dependencies.  (did I say that in a clear way?)  Possibly it could be something like this.

sourceCpp('../calculatePercentClearenceParallel.cpp')

shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {

    # This would include the variables that affect both plots and would execute the long running function (myFunction)
    addExecutionNode('LongRunningFunction', dependsOn = NA, outputEnvironment = output, {
      mslope = tan(input$slider_mslope*((2*pi)/360))

      tpc = myFunction(nm = nm)
    })

    # This would include the variables that affect this plot only and would not need to execute the long running function...
    addExecutionNode('Plot1', dependsOn = c('LongRunningFunction', outputEnvironment = output, {
      mslope = tan(input$slider_mslope*((2*pi)/360))

      pdata = tpc$PCData1

      rp1 = ggplot(pdata) + theme_bw() +
        geom_tile(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, fill = pc)) +
        geom_contour(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, z = smoothpc), breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8), color = 'red') +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = range(pdata$slopes), ylim = range(pdata$intercepts))
      rp1
    })

    addExecutionNode('Plot2', dependsOn = c('LongRunningFunction', outputEnvironment = output, {
      mslope = tan(input$slider_mslope*((2*pi)/360))

      pdata = tpc$PCData2

      rp2 = ggplot(pdata) + theme_bw() +
        geom_tile(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, fill = pc)) +
        geom_contour(aes(x = slopes, y = intercepts, z = smoothpc), breaks = c(0.4, 0.6, 0.8), color = 'red') +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
        coord_cartesian(xlim = range(pdata$slopes), ylim = range(pdata$intercepts))
      rp2
    })
  }
)

messages.subject: save DataTable state or row selections
messages.subject_clean: save DataTable state or row selections
messages.body_plain:
Hello.

I'm trying to write an application in which the user can select an arbitrary set of rows in a DataTable by clicking on a row or a checkbox in the row to toggle the row selection state.  The table is long and pageable.

In my initial attempts I stored the visual selection indicator in the DataTable and sent it to R using Shiny.onInputChange.  This didn't work because of the server-side DataTable processing; as the user paged the table R knew what was selected but the visual selection indicators got lost since Shiny didn't know about them.

My second attempt stores the selection indicator in a column in the table and re-renders the table whenever there's a change in the selection state.  Unfortunately this doesn't work either, because while the state indicator does get displayed properly there is other user state in the DataTable (page number, number of rows per page, filter values, search value) which gets lost when the table is re-rendered.

DataTables has a stateSave option which looked like it might fix this but unfortunately setting it didn't help.  I suspect this has something to do with how the Shiny server-side processing works.

There are also stateSaveCallback and stateLoadCallback options, but my attempts to use the first just hang up the browser and I'm not even sure what I would do with the second.

I might be able to work around the problem by making the table non-pageable and moving the filter boxes to the top (I haven't tried this but presumably it's possible) but it's not ideal.

Does anyone have a solution to the big problem, which is keeping row-selection synchronized between R and the visual selection indicator in a pageable DataTable without disturbing the DataTable?

Or a way to save/restore the DataTable state?

Or maybe just a better way to do row selection?

Thanks,
Ron

Is this all the code? I don't see input$adate anywhere...

Anyway, on inspection, your server.R needs to be refactored into "reactive" style. Example:

  BirthDate=as.POSIXlt(input$date)
needs to become
  BirthDate=reactive(as.POSIXlt(input$date))

and then you access the BirthDate value by calling it like a function: BirthDate()

Also this whole chunk that generates BirthDate_Table needs to be rewritten like this:

BirthDate_Table=reactive({
  result=data.frame(Birthday=as.POSIXlt(character()))

  counter=1

  birthDate=BirthDate()
  while(birthDate<Today){
    result[counter,]=as.character(birthDate)
    birthDate$year=birthDate$year+1
    counter=counter+1
  }

  result$Day=strftime(result$Birthday,"%A")
  result$Age=0:(nrow(result)-1)
  result$count=1
  return(result)
})

and similarly, any other reactive or output that needs to access BirthDate_Table would call BirthDate_Table().

See http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/lesson6/ for more information.

messages.subject: Re: shinysky - Confirm alert does not work
messages.subject_clean: shinysky - Confirm alert does not work
messages.body_plain:
@Micahel Frank.

I think I have found a (hacky and probably not recommended) solution in ShinySky.

The solution has nothing to do with ShinySky per se but has a lot to do with how Shiny works.

I think when you create a button like that dynamically using pure HTML Shiny actually doesn't know that it exists. From this page <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html> of the Shiny tutorial we see that it is recommended that we run shiny.unbindAll(); before we insert a new dynamic component and shiny.bindAll() after. I think bindAll() will run some code that scans the HTML DOM for shiny componenents and makes it available for use. So that's what I have done.

Solution Code

library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(

    shinyalert("idTestAlert", auto.close.after = 105, click.hide = F),

    actionButton("idTestBtn", "Show Alert"),
    verbatimTextOutput("idText")),
  server = function(session, input, output) {
    btnCounter <- reactive({

      browser()

      if (is.null(input[["idTest"]])) 0
      else input[["idTest"]]
    })
    observe({
      if (input$idTestBtn>0)
        showshinyalert(session,
                       "idTestAlert",

                       HTML("<script>Shiny.unbindAll();  </script>Test <button id='idTest' type='button' class='btn action-button btn-warning'>Confirm</button> <script>Shiny.bindAll();</script>"),

                       styleclass="warning")
    })

    output$idText <- renderText({btnCounter()})
  }
)

I had unexpected difficulty displaying different vAxis labels based on selectInput selections on a gvisScatterChart in a Shiny app.

The problem apparently was providing the vAxis "title" attribute of the gvisScatterChart() options list with a properly formatted JSON string.

With the help of an SO answer -- noted in the code snippet below -- I finally managed to do this by building a JSON string with the RJSONIO package's toJSON() method. This is indicated in bold in the relevant code snippet below from the server.R script.

Although this works, I had to (re-)cast a variable that already was a character with as.character(), so I'm wondering if I've made a (simple?) mistake that might catch up with me later.

I'll appreciate any insight on a better/standard way to do this.

# ---- from server.R ----

:
:
library(RJSONIO)
:
:
output$googleView <- renderGvis({

# filter the original dataset for the current raceway selection
  filtered.data <- myData %>% filter(tank %in% cbData())

# get the index of the current WQ property selection from nameToCode
# FYI, nameToCode is a list that collects display-able strings of water quality parameters
  idx<-which(nameToCode == input$mySelect)

# build a test data frame
  test.data.df<-data.frame(x=1:138,y=filtered.data[idx+1])

# NB: must build a JSON string for dynamic title of vAxis
# see: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14080344/gvisscatterchart-define-series-dynamically

# Build JSON string, casting a character -- codeToName[idx] -- as a...character?!
myVAxis <- toJSON(list(title=as.character(codeToName[idx])))  # this works...

cat(myVAxis,'\n')
# example output of call to cat()
# {
# "title": "pH (NBS)"
# }

  gvisScatterChart(test.data.df,
                   options=list(title=paste(codeToNameRw[idxRw],codeToName[idx],'(2012)'),
                               vAxis=myVAxis,
                                hAxis="{title:'2012'}",
                                width=500,height=400)
                                )
})

messages.subject: Support for DataTable DT_RowId
messages.subject_clean: Support for DataTable DT_RowId
messages.body_plain:
I don't think Shiny currently supports the DataTable DT_RowId feature which allows the server to specify unique row id's that DataTable places on the tr elements as id attributes. (http://www.datatables.net/examples/server_side/ids.html) <http://www.datatables.net/examples/server_side/ids.html>
This would be a very useful feature for applications where the client needs to communicate with the server about specific rows in the table.  It makes row identification logic much cleaner on both client and server and removes the current limitation that the visible columns in the table must contain sufficient information to uniquely identify the row.

Currently when a user clicks on a table row my application client code needs to pull data from a set of td elements that constitute a unique row identifier and send this back to R, and then the R code has to match this to the data frame.  It would be cleaner if R could specify e.g. the row.names or row numbers as DT_RowId in renderDataTable and then just pull them off the tr's and send them back to R.

Ron

messages.subject: Professional R Shiny App
messages.subject_clean: Professional R Shiny App
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was wondering if anyone knew of any examples of professional r shiny applications (for sale). I've been working on an R shiny application for the past 5 months or so, and want to eventually sell licenses for people to access it. I was wondering if this is a reasonable goal - I understand I will need to get the R shiny Pro server eventually (can't afford it at the moment), and speed is also an issue so I would be interested in parallelizing a lot of the code.

I'm a little concerned that R shiny isn't really built for this sort of thing, but right now I can't see any downsides besides the speed issue. It does some pretty computationally intense things (like running random forest hundreds of times, k-means clustering, etc), so I'm not sure what most users would be expecting.

Thanks,
Luke
